notes: RBox edit that removes a property the relation really has (coordinator rule: no added properties). Derived queries state the instance facts in the prompt and ask what follows, so they are determinate by construction and carry no determinacy. Yes/no answers are balanced across the topic's RBox records through phrasing ('does it follow ...?' against 'given only this fact, is it possible ...?'). Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. All instance facts are clear in the real world (R1). Functionality of in_genus holds without exception: under the zoological and botanical codes a species name is a binomen, one genus name plus one epithet, so a species is placed in exactly one genus at a time (taxonomists may disagree about WHICH genus, but no classification puts a species in two). Subgenera and nothogenera are single placements too. The second genus in the first instance is Acinonyx (the cheetah's genus), not Felis, because Linnaeus named the lion Felis leo, which could make 'the lion belongs to Felis' look partly true (R1). The near query asks the same property of has_type_species: each nominal genus has exactly one type species.
